missionPremise: pe-tokens.css states the line vocabulary by ROLE: --ss-line-06 #414247 rules INSIDE a surface, --ss-line-14 #56575C the edge OF a surface, --ss-line-28 #8A8A8F focus / outline buttons / emphasis. SettingsModal.tsx paints structure with the emphasis token ten times, so the surface reads white beside the docks, which use line06/line14 correctly. This is a misused semantic, not a taste call.
completionPredicate: Every line usage on the Settings surface carries the token its ROLE calls for; a file-shaped test asserts no structural line28 remains in the Settings tree and has been shown to fail in both directions; tsc clean, vitest green, chrome-kit gate exit 0; the visual outcome is explicitly NOT claimed.
scopeBasis: Dispatch scopes the Settings surface. The shared Card/Modal shell is in scope because the operator named the outer edge and the dispatch authorises a shared-shell change once the blast radius is reported. Dock, rail and map chrome are the reference and are untouched. Four hand-rolled modal shells carrying the same defect are named, NOT changed.

instrument.what: WCAG contrast of each line token against each ground plane
instrument.selfTest: 5/5 including one NOT-VACUOUS negative (must refuse 4.5 for a pair it scores 3.017)
instrument.independentDerivation: pe-tokens.css records, from a different author on a different date, that line-28 on the lifted --ss-raised measures 3.017. The instrument reproduces 3.017 exactly. That is a second source of truth, not internal consistency.

principalFinding.claim: The line ladder is calibrated against the DOCK plane --ss-ink #323234, but the Settings modal sits on the RAISED plane --ss-raised-98 #3F4043, where line06 is 1.034 — effectively invisible.
principalFinding.mechanism: This explains WHY the author reached one rung up on everything in this file: on the raised plane the semantically-correct internal-rule token disappears, so they used line14 for rules and line28 for edges. The compensation was reasonable at the bottom and overshot at the top, where line28 at 3.017 is the brightest line in the palette.
principalFinding.rejectedAlternative: That SettingsModal was simply authored carelessly against the vocabulary. Rejected: careless authorship would scatter, and this file is INTERNALLY consistent (every edge line28, every rule line14) — it is a systematic one-rung shift, which is a compensation, not a slip.
principalFinding.consequenceIShipAnyway: Assigning the ROLE-correct token sends seven structural rules to line06 at 1.034, i.e. near-invisible on this ground. I ship the role anyway and declare the measurement, because choosing line14 for a rule BECAUSE line06 is invisible would encode a palette defect into fifteen call sites — the fallback-so-the-code-does-not-raise pattern ENFORCEMENT bans. The raise is correct behaviour.
principalFinding.precedentThatThisIsAlreadyTheShippedStat: Modal.tsx L87 already paints its header rule with line06 on this exact ground (1.034) and has shipped that way unremarked. The kit own shell already does what I am about to do one element higher.
principalFinding.ifTheOperatorsEyeDisagrees: The fix is palette-level — a line step calibrated for --ss-raised, or dropping the modal fill to --ss-ink — NOT a re-tune of these call sites. pe-tokens.css sets this precedent itself for the hover 7 percent: that is a palette-author question and belongs in a request, not in a re-tune here.

classification.rule: A line is an EDGE when it bounds a distinct region; a RULE when it divides content on one plane; EMPHASIS when it signals rather than structures.
classification.gapInTheVocabulary: Settings is built from a component the kit does not have: an UNFILLED outlined group box on the raised plane. The three-token vocabulary assumes a box is either a filled surface (edge, line14) or a divider on a plane (line06). The author closed that gap by reaching up a rung. I close it by treating an outlined group as the edge of a bounded region -> line14.

theOneLeftAlone.why: It is the only line in the file that SIGNALS rather than STRUCTURES. The other fourteen say these are separate; this one says read this differently. The author made it 2px where every other rule in the file is 1px, i.e. deliberately a different KIND of line. It is also not on the operator list (outer edge, tab underline, row rules, rail divider).
theOneLeftAlone.counterReadingRejected: That an Aside carries quiet secondary content (t4 text) so the brightest line in the palette inverts its hierarchy, and quiet-surfaces-loud-exceptions makes an Aside a quiet surface. Rejected on the 2px signal and the operator omission, but it is genuinely close: this is a one-token change at one call site if the operator eye disagrees.
theOneLeftAlone.doubleCheckDemanded: The dispatch warns a report finding ZERO legitimate line28 uses is suspicious. It does not find zero. Four legitimate uses render ON the Settings surface and are untouched: Button.tsx:50 primary = the quiet OUTLINE BUTTON (verbatim in the token doc), StatusChip.tsx:42,56 dashed absence chips, pe-tokens.css:283 .pe-btn:hover border, pe-tokens.css:316 rail bubble hover. Every one is a control state, which is what the token means.

blastRadius.question: Does the Settings outer edge come from Modal.tsx or SettingsModal.tsx?
blastRadius.answer: NEITHER paints it. Modal.tsx renders <Card raised>, and Card.tsx:22 paints the 1px line28 outer edge. Modal.tsx own contribution is its header rule at L87, which is ALREADY line06 and correct.
blastRadius.cardConsumers: Card has exactly ONE consumer repo-wide: components/Modal.tsx (grep across apps + packages). Card NON-raised branch has ZERO consumers and is dead code — reported, not deleted, as out of scope.
blastRadius.modalConsumers: Modal has exactly TWO consumers: browse/SettingsModal.tsx and components/PdfViewer.tsx.
soChangingCardTouches: PdfViewer outer edge (NOT asked for — declared)

falsifierThatFired.preRegistered: If any file paints a modal-shaped surface WITHOUT Card, my blast-radius claim is wrong.
falsifierThatFired.result: IT FIRED. Four more modal shells hand-roll the same chrome (rModal + modalBg + shModal) and carry the SAME line28 outer edge, and my change does NOT reach them: browse/PricingModal.tsx:191, checkout/CheckoutPage.tsx:90, checkout/UnlockCheckoutModal.tsx:77, coldopen/SignUpCard.tsx:80.
falsifierThatFired.consequence: modal-edge-equals-line28 is an app-wide convention spelled six times, not a Settings slip. My scoped change corrects 2 of 6 and leaves 4 inconsistent. I do NOT widen — the dispatch scopes me to Settings — and I name the four with line numbers as a follow-on for the planner.
falsifierThatFired.whyThisMattersMoreThanTheFix: The dispatch anticipated a shared shell whose blast radius was too WIDE. The measured risk is the opposite: the shell is too NARROW to carry the convention, so the app cannot be corrected through it.
